subject: DONE s337b (73d43ac): part 1 s318 (runner skip dropped), part 2 s337b (four drifted copies restored + triaged)
description:
PART 1 DONE s318 (234afa3): the basename+head "already in the sweep corpus" skip is gone from tools/run-perl-suite.pl; need-harness is the only filter; 91 files became visible.

PART 2 DONE s337b (73d43ac).  perl-tests/{chop,dor,not,quotemeta}.t restored byte-identical to t/op/.  They had been EDITED IN PLACE — plan counts hand-lowered (chop 148->100, not 24->20, quotemeta 60->56) and dor.t replaced outright by a hand-written "Simplified from Perl's t/op/dor.t" (34 rows -> 9).  Every newly-visible failure carries a cause:

- not.t 21-24 -> skip registry :read-only (interned !0/!1: one shared read-only scalar in perl, a fresh mutable value in PCL).  #159 gave ARRAYS a read-only representation; a read-only SCALAR still has nowhere to carry the flag.
- dor.t 26/28 -> skip registry :principle9 (`f $x /2`, `print $fh /2` must die "Search pattern not terminated" — assert rejection of invalid Perl).  Siblings with `/ 2` pass and are unmatched by the regexes.
- quotemeta.t 30/31 -> fail-baseline rows taken verbatim from the faillog; owned by #146.
- chop.t -> PARTIAL 96+0/148.  CAUSE (probed): utf8::encode is a NO-OP in PCL — `utf8::encode("\x{100}")` stays 1 char of ord 256 where perl yields bytes 196,128 — so chop.t's own `next if $end_utf8 eq $end` guard always fires and 48 rows are NEVER EMITTED.  Not skip-registrable.  The old plan of exactly 100 had been masking the shortfall.  Written up in not-supported.md under 'Unicode semantics differences' as a second-order consequence.

BONUS, verified: #159 turned op/push.t, op/splice.t, op/unshift.t from DIFF to OK in the perl suite — three of this task's own near-green candidates (their single divergent row was the read-only one).

Baselines: pass-baseline.tsv updated for the 4 files; 2 rows added to fail-baseline.tsv by hand.  Gate 131/4594 PASS; sweep 18498 passing / 681 fails, GATE clean, 0 new.  Fully-passing 66 -> 64 (chop.t and quotemeta.t stopped over-claiming) — that is the intended outcome.

REMAINING (not part of this task): docs/perl-suite-run.tsv still predates part 1 and has no rows for the 91 newly-visible files; a full re-run grows it by ~91 rows.  The near-green list in the s318 data is still worth mining (op/args, context, crypt, exists_sub, print, wantarray, time each 1 row off).
